editorial:
Full Metal Jacket follows a group of young Marine recruits through the brutal boot camp training at Parris Island and then into the chaos of the Vietnam War. You meet Private Joker, a smart-mouthed recruit who becomes a war correspondent, and his fellow soldiers as they are pushed to their breaking points by a terrifying drill instructor. The movie has a raw, gritty feel that pulls you right into the madness of war and the way it changes people.

The acting is incredible, especially the drill instructor who steals every scene he is in. The boot camp half is intense and unforgettable, while the second half drops you into street fighting in Hue with a slower, more tense pace. Some viewers might find the second half less gripping than the first, but the whole film is a powerful look at how war strips away humanity. If you enjoy classic war dramas with strong characters, this is a must-see.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Joker and his squad hunt down a sniper in the ruins of Hue. They discover the sniper is a young Vietnamese woman. After she is wounded, Joker shoots her to end her suffering. The squad walks off into the sunset singing the Mickey Mouse Club theme song, showing how they have become numb to the horror around them. It is a dark, unsettling ending that leaves you thinking.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves classic war dramas with strong characters
